newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end higher with help of U.S. mkt.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end higher with help of U.S. mkt.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished higher Thursday guided by strong performance by U.S. Treasuries.

"The Argentine market is accompanying U.S. markets higher," said a trader at an Argentine bank. U.S. Treasuries were boosted by a well received five-year bond auction which helped sustain earlier gains. The yield on the 30-year U.S. Treasury fell 10 basis points to 6.59 percent.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.15 to 122.15, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 rose 7/8 to 86-1/8.
Argentina's Brady bonds were the main gainers of the session, showing their customary larger correlation with the U.S. markets than local instruments.

The market was also helped by the signing of three decrees on labor market reforms by President Carlos Menem late Wednesday. Analysts said considering the long wait for the reforms, it was welcome news that Menem finally decided to go ahead with decrees rather than waiting longer to muster congressional support for the measures.
"The measures are especially good for markets," said Roberto Costa Bourdieu, senior fixed income analyst at Banco Rio.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 7.05 percent from 7.50 percent.
